organizations.publicNote: German record company established in Berlin in 1900. Grammophon and Polydor were record-label imprints and are represented separately from the corporate body.
Record-label imprint of Deutsche Grammophon-Aktiengesellschaft, printed as Polydor on the linked German and export issues.

sources.researchNote: The upload title’s “(1927)” is the year of the song, not of the recording. The Ben Berlin discography at grammophon-platten.de lists Polydor 21768 (“Miss Annabelle Lee” / “Ice-Cream”) without a date, directly beside Polydor 21769, dated July 1928, and the duo’s Polydor 21898 as September 1928; the issue is therefore dated [1928].

works.title: Le bistrot du port
works.publicNote: Valse written for the singer Lys Gauty, to words by Gaston Groener and A. Saudemont; the printed edition (Paris: Coda, cop. 1934) credits the music to Pierre Candel, a pseudonym standing here for Kaper and Jurmann together. In his 1975 AFI oral history Kaper recalled it as the last song he wrote in Paris, and said he never heard it there before leaving for the United States.
